questions.q: Why is ServiceNow usually described as a "system of action" rather than a "system of record"?
options: It's the platform where processes actually run, get approved, and get closed — but the underlying data it needs usually lives in other systems like Workday, Salesforce, or monitoring tools
ServiceNow cannot store any data of its own
It is always the authoritative source for every type of data an enterprise uses
"System of record" and "system of action" mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: ServiceNow drives the process, but the authoritative data (employee records, infrastructure state, customer accounts) typically lives elsewhere — which is exactly why integration matters.

questions.q: What real business cost does manual re-entry between ServiceNow and an external system create?
options: None — manual re-entry is just as fast and reliable as integration
Delay, data drift, and typo risk, because a human has to notice and re-type data that already exists somewhere else
It eliminates the need for any integration at all
It only affects very large enterprises, never mid-size companies
questions.explain: Every manual hand-off is a point where data can arrive late, get mistyped, or drift out of sync between the two systems.

questions.q: A monitoring tool detects a server outage and automatically creates a ServiceNow Incident without a human logging it. Which direction of integration is this?
options: Outbound — ServiceNow is calling out to the monitoring tool
Not integration at all, since no REST call is involved
Inbound — an external system is pushing data into ServiceNow, triggered by an event outside ServiceNow
Bidirectional polling, since both systems check each other constantly
questions.explain: The trigger originates outside ServiceNow (the monitoring tool detecting the outage), and that external system pushes the resulting data in — the defining trait of an inbound integration.

questions.q: What decides whether a given ServiceNow integration should be built as inbound or outbound, according to this lesson?
options: Whichever direction is more convenient or faster for the developer to build
The programming language used on the external system
The size of the company running the integration
Where the triggering event actually happens — inside ServiceNow or outside it
questions.explain: The direction follows the event: if the trigger happens outside ServiceNow (an outage, a new hire), the integration is inbound; if ServiceNow's own process triggers the need for outside action, it's outbound.

questions.q: Why does this course sit where it does in the ServiceNow Administrator → Developer → Technical Architect path, right after course 6 (Scripted REST APIs)?
options: It repeats the same Scripted REST API content from course 6 in more detail
Courses 1 through 6 built fluency inside ServiceNow itself; this course turns outward to build the pipes that connect ServiceNow to systems it doesn't own
It has no real connection to the courses before it in the path
It replaces the need for knowing how Scripted REST APIs work
questions.explain: This course is explicitly the turn from building and exposing data inside ServiceNow to integrating ServiceNow with the external systems that actually own the data it needs.
